findings.body:
**Resolve bare `gh` against absolute PATH entries before the cwd-scoped spawn.**

When `opts.cwd` is set, `gh` stays a bare name and the child inherits `PATH`. A relative or empty `PATH` entry can then resolve `gh` inside the spawn directory, so a repository that contains an executable named `gh` can run in place of the intended binary. The comment at lines 99-100 says bare names are cwd-independent. That holds only when every `PATH` entry is absolute.

Resolve bare names to absolute paths using the PATH walk in `src/driver/acp/binaries.ts` (resolves relative entries against the caller's cwd) before spawning, and pass that absolute path as `bin`. Then correct the comment at lines 99-100.
findings.title: Resolve bare `gh` against absolute PATH entries before the cwd-scoped spawn.

findings.body:
**Suppress `CQ_*` warnings in `--json` mode.**

Line 537 writes every `check.warningLines` entry to stderr. It does not check `rawMode`. The `--json` contract requires stderr to stay empty. An unknown or reserved `CQ_*` variable therefore adds stderr output to every `--json` run except `cq config`. The code comment at lines 512-518 states this is deliberate. Doctrine I1 contains no exception for it, so the code and the contract conflict. Either the code changes, or the owner amends I1 first.

<details>
<summary>🐛 Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-    for (const line of check.warningLines) io.stderr(`${line}\n`);
+    if (rawMode !== 'json') for (const line of check.warningLines) io.stderr(`${line}\n`);
```

</details>

The suppressed warnings are not lost. The comment at lines 516-518 says `cq config` reports the same diagnostics. Update the comment at lines 512-518 to match this change.
findings.title: Suppress `CQ` warnings in `--json` mode.

**Update the governance trigger docs in `run-plan.ts`.**

The header (lines 47-54) and the `runPlanThroughKernel` docstring (lines 297-298) say governance starts only when a cap is set. The code also enables governance for governance opt-ins. The header also says an uncapped run has no governor, which the opt-in path contradicts.

Lines 349-351 and 355-357 already state the implemented contract: a run with an opt-in is governed. The header and docstring need to match that contract.

<details>
<summary>Suggested doc fix</summary>

```diff
 // GOVERNED COMPOSITION (ADR-0003 §2, kernel README "Budget governor"): the
-// CLI opts into governance exactly when the operator sets a cap
-// (--max-usd/--max-tokens). A capped run carries a per-run governor
+// CLI opts into governance when the operator sets a cap
+// (--max-usd/--max-tokens) or a governance opt-in. A governed run carries a per-run governor
 // (createGovernor over governorConfig(runOptions, {})) and runPlan ITSELF
 // performs admission, spend observation, the honest stop (I9 — its return is
 // the final report; no post-pass), and the v2 journal; resume/ledger
 // seeding is the runner's fold over the journal dir, not a CLI step. An
-// UNCAPPED run stays v1-identical: no governor, no ledger, no v2 journal.
+// run with no cap and no opt-in stays v1-identical: no governor, no ledger, no v2 journal.
```

- * runCli-level DI override), the cap-keyed governance handle (the CLI governs
- * exactly when the operator set a cap — see the header), runPlan with the
+ * the registry view over the resolved ops root (the explicit --ops-root flag wins over the
+ * runCli-level DI override), the governance handle (the CLI governs when the
+ * operator sets a cap or a governance opt-in — see the header), runPlan with the

findings.body:
**Coerce numeric `--release-quarantine` job IDs to strings before validation.**

A single canonical-decimal job ID, such as `--release-quarantine=42`, reaches `releaseQuarantine` as the number `42`. The preprocess splits only strings, so the number passes through to `z.array(z.string().min(1))`, which rejects it. The run then fails as an input defect, and that job cannot be released. Comma-separated lists are unaffected because they remain strings.

The `JSON_VALUES_NOTE` text documents canonical-number parsing for plan flags, so the fix belongs in the `run-plan` schema rather than in `parseFlags`.

<details>
<summary>🐛 Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
     releaseQuarantine: z
       .preprocess(
-        (value) =>
-          typeof value === 'string'
-            ? value
-                .split(',')
-                .map((key) => key.trim())
-                .filter((key) => key !== '')
-            : value,
+        (value) => {
+          const text = typeof value === 'number' ? String(value) : value;
+          return typeof text === 'string'
+            ? text
+                .split(',')
+                .map((key) => key.trim())
+                .filter((key) => key !== '')
+            : text;
+        },
         z.array(z.string().min(1)),
       )
       .default([]),
```

</details>
findings.title: Coerce numeric `--release-quarantine` job IDs to strings before validation.

findings.body:
**Document the one-way format change for session rollback.**

The new `tool-failure` and `budget-stop` lines are not readable by a reader that predates them. Any session file that contains one of these lines fails to load in that reader, not only the diagnostic line. The format comment at `src/harness/session.ts:63-70` says only that old readers reject the new keys, and that there are none in old files. It does not cover the reverse direction.

<details>
<summary>📝 Suggested comment update</summary>

```diff
-  * old readers reject only these NEW keys — there are none in
-  * old files.
+  * old readers reject these NEW keys. A reader that predates the
+  * `tool-failure` and `budget-stop` line types throws `corrupt line`
+  * for the whole session when it finds one. Do not run an older
+  * toolkit version against a sessions directory that holds these lines.
```

</details>
findings.title: Document the one-way format change for session rollback.

findings.body:
**A final-step context-ceiling trip turns a valid structured result into `budget`.**

`onStepFinish` records a meter trip on every step, including the last. When the last answering step carries input at or above `maxContextTokens`, `stopReasonOf` returns `'budget'` before it checks `finishReason`. The `complete` gate then drops the validated `structuredOutput`. The `Budget.maxContextTokens` contract stops the run "before the next request." After a final answer, no next request exists, so the trip should not override a natural finish. Limit the meter override to runs that would send another request, and add a loop test for a final-step trip.
findings.title: A final-step context-ceiling trip turns a valid structured result into `budget`.
